The '''2007–08 Premier League''' (known as the '''[[Barclays]] Premier League''' for sponsorship reasons) season was the 16th since its establishment. The first matches of the season were played on 11 August 2007, and the season ended on 11 May 2008. [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] went into the 2007–08 season as the Premier League's defending champions, having won their ninth Premier League title and sixteenth league championship overall the previous season. This season was also the third consecutive season to see the "[[Big Six (Premier League)|Big Four]]" continue their stranglehold on the top four spots (which mean [[UEFA Champions League]] qualification).

==Overview==
The first goal of the season was scored by [[Michael Chopra]], who scored a 94th-minute winner for [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham]] in the early kick-off.<ref name="first_goal">{{cite news |first=Andrew |last=McKenzie |title=Sunderland 1–0 Tottenham |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/6931064.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=11 August 2007|access-date=25 September 2007}}</ref> The first red card of the season was given to [[Reading F.C.|Reading]]'s [[Dave Kitson]] after a challenge on [[Patrice Evra]] in their opening game against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].<ref name="kitson_redcard">{{cite news |first=John |last=Sinnott |title=Man Utd 0–0 Reading |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/6931068.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=12 August 2007|access-date=25 September 2007}}</ref> The first [[hat-trick]] was scored by [[Emmanuel Adebayor]] in the match between [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]].<ref name="first_hattrick">{{cite news |first=Ian |last=Hughes |title=Arsenal 5–0 Derby |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/6996740.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=22 September 2007|access-date=25 September 2007}}</ref>

On 29 September 2007, [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] and [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] played the [[List of highest-scoring Premier League games|highest-scoring match in Premier League history]], in which Portsmouth [[Portsmouth F.C. 7–4 Reading F.C.|won 7–4]].<ref name="portsmouth_sevenfour">{{cite news |first=Stuart |last=Roach |title=Portsmouth 7–4 Reading |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7008200.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=29 September 2007|access-date=1 October 2007| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20071013010728/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7008200.stm| archive-date= 13 October 2007| url-status= live}}</ref> On 15 December 2007, both [[Roque Santa Cruz]] ([[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]]) and [[Marcus Bent]] ([[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]]) scored [[hat-trick]]s during Wigan's 5–3 home win over Blackburn. This was the first occasion in Premier League history that two players on opposing teams had scored hat-tricks during the same match.<ref name=ThreeHistory>{{cite news |first=Martin |last=Tyler |title=Three and history|url=http://www.skysports.com/opinion/story/0,25212,12038_6390475,00.html |publisher=Sky Sports |date=20 September 2010| access-date= 21 March 2011}}</ref>

Manchester United successfully defended their title, winning tenth Premier League on the final day with a 2–0 win over Wigan Athletic, while second-placed [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] drew 1–1 with [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]]. It was their seventeenth English title overall, with the club just one title behind [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|their rivals]] [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]'s total of 18. Elsewhere on the final day, [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] thrashed [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] 8–1 to claim the biggest win of the season.

On 29 March 2008, [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] drew 2–2 with [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] while [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]], who were 17th in the table at the time, beat [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] 3–1, to make Derby County the first team in Premier League history to be relegated in March.<ref name=Woeful>{{cite news |first=Jonathan|last=Stephenson |title=Where do woeful Derby rank?|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/d/derby_county/4856682.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=29 March 2008| access-date= 21 March 2011}}</ref> Throughout the season, the team won just one game and recorded only 11 points, the lowest tally in top flight history. On the final day of the season, Reading beat Derby 4–0 and Birmingham City beat Blackburn Rovers 4–1. However, Fulham's 1–0 win over Portsmouth sent both teams down as the London club avoided the drop on goal difference.

The season was notable for the return of the English league to the top of [[UEFA coefficient|UEFA's official ranking list]], overtaking [[La Liga]] for the period from 1 May 2008 to 30 April 2009. This followed the success of English clubs in the [[UEFA Champions League]], with both champions Manchester United and runners-up Chelsea reaching the [[2008 UEFA Champions League final|final]]. This was the first time that the English league had topped the UEFA rankings since the [[Heysel Stadium disaster]] in 1985.

==Teams==
Twenty teams competed in the league&nbsp;– the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[2006–07 Football League Championship|Championship]]. The promoted teams were [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]], [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] (both teams returning after a season's  absence), and [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] (returning after a five-year absence). They replaced [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]], [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] and [[Watford F.C.|Watford]]. The previous season had seen Sheffield United and Watford both suffer an immediate return to the [[2007–08 Football League Championship|Championship]], while Charlton Athletic were relegated after a seven-year top flight spell.

In addition, Premier League officials were supplied with new kit made by [[Umbro]], replacing American makers Official Sports, and were sponsored by [[AirAsia]], replacing Emirates. The 2007–08 season saw a new font used for the names on the back of players' shirts.<ref>{{cite web |date=12 June 2007|url=http://www.football-shirts.co.uk/fans/new-premier-league-name-number-style_162 |title=New Premier League name & number style |work=football-shirts.co.uk |access-date=25 January 2009| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090208162529/http://www.football-shirts.co.uk/fans/new-premier-league-name-number-style_162| archive-date= 8 February 2009| url-status= dead}}</ref>

=== Records ===
* [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] finished with the worst record since the league was founded in [[1992–93 FA Premier League|1992–93]] and also the worst since the introduction of the three points for a win rule. Among the records set by the Rams were:
** A final record of one win, eight draws and 29 losses for a total of eleven points, worse than the [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] team from [[2005–06 FA Premier League|2005–06]], with the previously set lows of three wins, six draws and 29 losses totalling fifteen points. The single win, coming at home against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] 1–0 on 17 September was also a record for the fewest wins in a Premier League campaign
** Derby's 20 goals scored as a team (with Ronaldo, Adebayor and Torres each scoring more goals individually) was lower than the [[2002–03 FA Premier League|2002–03]] Black Cats' total with 21 goals scored. This marked the third time a team was outscored by one or more players. The team also failed to score in 21 of their 38 games
** Their −69 goal difference (20 goals scored, 89 conceded) was worse than [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]]'s [[1994–95 FA Premier League|1994–95]] goal difference of −57 (36 goals scored, 93 conceded). The 89 goals they conceded was the worst defensive performance by a team since Ipswich Town conceded 93 goals in 1994–95. It was also the worst record since the Premier League adopted the 20-team, 38-match format in 1995–96
** The 29 defeats they suffered equalled the 2005–06 Sunderland team for the most losses suffered in one Premier League season
* Chelsea's 85 points accumulated was a new record for the most points gained in a 38-game season without securing the title. The 83 points achieved by Arsenal was a new record for the most points gained in a 38-game season for finishing third
* Manchester United's goal difference of +58 was the greatest ever attained in a Premier League season, beating the record set by Chelsea in [[2004–05 FA Premier League|2004–05]]
* [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] beat his own record for most goals scored by a midfielder, raising the record to 31 goals. The previous record was 17 goals, from the [[2006–07 FA Premier League|previous season]]. Furthermore, his goal total equalled the highest number of goals ever scored in the Premier League during a 38-game season, equalling the record first set by Blackburn Rovers' [[Alan Shearer]] during the [[1995–96 FA Premier League|1995–96 season]]
* [[Marcus Bent]] and [[Roque Santa Cruz]] each scored a hat trick for their team during [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]]'s 5–3 victory over [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] on 15 December 2007. This is the first time in Premier League history that players from opposing sides both scored hat-tricks in the same match<ref name=ThreeHistory/>
* [[Emmanuel Adebayor]] scored two hat tricks home and away against Derby. This was the first time in the Premier League that a player had scored a hat trick against the same team twice in the league
* [[Fernando Torres]] scored 24 goals for Liverpool, a new record for goals scored by a foreign player during his debut season<ref>{{cite news |first=Martin |last=Isaacs |title=Fernando Torres breaks record in Liverpool win |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/main.jhtml?view=DETAILS&grid=A1YourView&xml=/sport/2008/05/12/sfgtot112.xml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080515194426/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/main.jhtml?view=DETAILS&grid=A1YourView&xml=%2Fsport%2F2008%2F05%2F12%2Fsfgtot112.xml |url-status=dead |archive-date=15 May 2008 |work=Telegraph.co.uk |date=12 May 2008 |access-date=12 May 2008 }}</ref>
